enunciation: A (classical) quiver is a quadruple Gamma=(V,E,s,t): a finite vertex set V, a finite edge set E, and maps s,t: E -> V giving each edge a source and a target.
hypotheses: V finite; E finite
conclusion: the data (V,E,s,t) with s,t : E -> V

enunciation: An (etale) K-rational structure on a quiver Gamma is a group homomorphism rho: Gal(L/K) -> Aut(Gamma) for a Galois extension L/K such that the induced actions on V and E are continuous for the discrete topologies; Gamma_K := (Gamma,rho) is a quiver over K.
quantifiers: for a Galois extension L/K (finite or infinite)
hypotheses: Gamma=(V,E,s,t) a classical quiver; L/K Galois
conclusion: rho a group hom into Aut(Gamma) with continuous (hence smooth) actions on the discrete sets V and E; equivalently rho_V, rho_E continuous with s,t Gal-equivariant (eq:stgaloisequivariance)

enunciation: Gamma_K=(Gamma,rho) is constant / split over K iff rho is the trivial homomorphism, i.e. the Gal(L/K)-actions on V and on E are both trivial.
hypotheses: Gamma_K a quiver over K
conclusion: rho trivial; equivalently both induced actions trivial

enunciation: A homomorphism phi: Gamma_K -> Gamma'_K of quivers over K is a homomorphism of the underlying quivers which commutes with the Gal(K^sep/K)-actions on Gamma_K and Gamma'_K.
quantifiers: for Gamma_K, Gamma'_K quivers over K
hypotheses: Gamma_K, Gamma'_K quivers over K (rational structures inflated to Gal(K^sep/K), cf. RQ2-1.20)
conclusion: phi is a quiver homomorphism Gamma -> Gamma' (compatible with s and t) AND commutes with the two Gal(K^sep/K)-actions

enunciation: For Gamma_K=(Gamma,rho) with rho an action of Gal(L/K) and any intermediate field L/E'/K with E'/K finite, the base change is the E'-rational quiver Gamma_{E'} = E' tensor_K Gamma_K := (Gamma, rho restricted to Gal(L/E')).
quantifiers: for any intermediate field L/E'/K with E'/K finite
hypotheses: Gamma_K=(Gamma,rho) an action of Gal(L/K); E'/K finite
conclusion: Gamma_{E'} := (Gamma, rho|_{Gal(L/E')}) is an E'-rational quiver
scope_note: v1 RQ-1.05 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: For L/E'/K with E'/K finite and an E'-rational quiver Gamma_{E'}=(Gamma,rho) with Gamma=(V,E,s,t), the restriction res_{E'/K} Gamma_{E'} is the quiver (Gal(L/K) x_{Gal(L/E')} V, Gal(L/K) x_{Gal(L/E')} E, Gal(L/K) x_{Gal(L/E')} s, Gal(L/K) x_{Gal(L/E')} t).

hypotheses: E'/K finite; Gamma_{E'}=(Gamma,rho) an E'-rational quiver
conclusion: the induced-set quiver on Gal(L/K) x_{Gal(L/E')} (-) applied to V, E, s, t; it is a K-rational quiver

enunciation: A K-rational representation M_K of Gamma_K consists of (i) L-vector spaces M(v) for v in V, (ii) semi-linear isomorphisms varphi_{v,sigma}: M(v) -> M(sigma v) satisfying the cocycle condition eq:semi-linearactiononrep and such that the resulting Gal(L/K)-action on the disjoint union of the M(v) is CONTINUOUS (vacuous for finite L/K), and (iii) L-linear maps phi_e: M(s(e)) -> M(t(e)) compatible with the Galois action via eq:koecheractiononrep.
quantifiers: for each v in V and each sigma in Gal(L/K); for each e in E
hypotheses: Gamma_K a quiver over K with respect to a Galois extension L/K
conclusion: the three data (i),(ii),(iii) together with the cocycle condition, the CONTINUITY of the action on the disjoint union of the M(v), and the edge-equivariance condition
scope_note: v1 RQ-1.08 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: A homomorphism of K-rational representations M,N is a classical homomorphism (psi_v: M(v) -> N(v))_v over L compatible with the rational structures varphi^M on M and varphi^N on N: psi_{sigma v} o varphi^M_{v,sigma} = varphi^N_{v,sigma} o psi_v (eq:koecheractiononrephom).
quantifiers: for all v in V and all sigma in Gal(L/K)
hypotheses: M=(M(v))_v and N=(N(v))_v K-rational representations of Gamma_K
conclusion: psi is a homomorphism of the underlying classical L-representations AND satisfies eq:koecheractiononrephom
scope_note: v1 RQ-1.09 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: Rep(Gamma_K) is the category of finite-dimensional K-rational representations of Gamma_K; Rep^nil(Gamma_K) is the full subcategory of finite-dimensional nilpotent K-rational representations, where M_K is NILPOTENT if there is n >= 0 such that phi_p := phi_{e_m} o ... o phi_{e_1} = 0 for every path p = e_m...e_1 in Gamma of length m >= n (a property of the underlying classical representation over L).
quantifiers: for a K-rational quiver Gamma_K
hypotheses: Gamma_K a K-rational quiver
conclusion: Rep(Gamma_K) is a category; Rep^nil(Gamma_K) is a FULL subcategory of it; both consist of FINITE-DIMENSIONAL objects; NILPOTENT is DEFINED: path composites of length >= n vanish for some n, a condition on the underlying classical representation
scope_note: v1 RQ-1.10 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: Let M_K = ((M(v))_v,(varphi_{v,sigma}),(phi_e)) be a (nilpotent) representation of a K-rational quiver Gamma_K and L/E'/K an intermediate field with E'/K finite. Then M_{E'} := E' tensor_K M_K := ((M(v))_v,(varphi_{v,sigma})_{v, sigma in Gal(L/E')},(phi_e)_e), obtained by RESTRICTING the semi-linear action to Gal(L/E'), is a (nilpotent) representation of E' tensor_K Gamma_K, and base change of (nilpotent) representations is functorial. If M_K is finite-dimensional the notation is justified by Galois descent: alpha tensor m -> alpha m is an isomorphism of E'-vector spaces E' tensor_K (oplus_v M(v))^{Gal(L/K)} = (oplus_v M(v))^{Gal(L/E')}.
quantifiers: for any intermediate field L/E'/K with E'/K FINITE (inserted by the r5 typo batch; cf. AN-19)
hypotheses: M_K a (nilpotent) representation of Gamma_K; for the descent isomorphism additionally M_K finite-dimensional
conclusion: M_{E'} is DEFINED by restricting the semi-linear action to Gal(L/E') (same spaces, same edge maps) and is a (nilpotent) representation of Gamma_{E'}; the assignment is functorial; for finite-dimensional M_K the canonical map E' tensor_K (oplus M(v))^{Gal(L/K)} -> (oplus M(v))^{Gal(L/E')} is an E'-linear ISOMORPHISM
scope_note: v1 RQ-1.11 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: For K-rational representations M_K,N_K of Gamma_K and any intermediate field L/E'/K with E'/K finite there is a canonical isomorphism E' tensor_K Hom_{Gamma_K}(M_K,N_K) = Hom_{Gamma_{E'}}(M_{E'},N_{E'}) of finite-dimensional E'-vector spaces.
quantifiers: for any intermediate field L/E'/K with E'/K FINITE (inserted by the r5 typo batch; cf. AN-19)
hypotheses: Gamma_K a quiver with a K-rational structure; M_K,N_K K-rational representations
conclusion: a CANONICAL isomorphism of finite-dimensional E'-vector spaces, for EVERY intermediate E' (not only E'=L)

enunciation: Galois descent: for L/K finite or infinite Galois, Vec_K is equivalent to the category of L-vector spaces with a K-structure -- the defining semi-linear action of Gal(L/K) being CONTINUOUS, as required by the definition of a K-structure -- and K-rational maps, via V -> (L tensor_K V, (varphi_sigma)), with quasi-inverse (V,(varphi_sigma)) -> V^{Gal(L/K)}.

hypotheses: L/K Galois (finite or infinite); the K-structure's semi-linear action is CONTINUOUS (explicitly named in the statement since the D2 source edit; vacuous for finite L/K)
conclusion: the stated functor is an equivalence of categories; V -> V^{Gal(L/K)} is a quasi-inverse; morphisms on the right are exactly the K-rational maps

enunciation: For L-vector spaces V,W each carrying a semi-linear Gal(L/K)-action, Gal(L/K) acts on Hom_L(V,W) by phi^sigma := sigma o phi o sigma^{-1}; IF the actions on V and W are continuous AND V is finite-dimensional over L, then this action is continuous for the discrete topology on Hom_L(V,W).

hypotheses: V,W L-vector spaces EACH endowed with a semi-linear Gal(L/K)-action; for the continuity claim additionally: both actions continuous AND V finite-dimensional over L
conclusion: phi^sigma := sigma o phi o sigma^{-1} is L-linear; this is a group action on Hom_L(V,W); CONDITIONALLY (continuous actions plus dim_L V finite) the action is continuous for the discrete topology

enunciation: A map phi: V -> W is semi-linear with respect to sigma in Gal(L/K) (sigma-linear) if phi(alpha . v) = sigma(alpha) phi(v) for all v in V and alpha in L.

hypotheses: sigma in Gal(L/K); V,W L-vector spaces

enunciation: A K-structure on an L-vector space V is a group homomorphism varphi: Gal(L/K) -> Aut_K(V), sigma -> varphi_sigma, such that each varphi_sigma is sigma-linear AND the resulting action Gal(L/K) x V -> V is CONTINUOUS for the discrete topology on V; explicitly, every v in V is fixed by varphi_sigma for all sigma in some open subgroup, and for finite L/K the condition is vacuous.
quantifiers: for each sigma in Gal(L/K)
hypotheses: V an L-vector space, viewed as a K-vector space via K -> L
conclusion: varphi is a group homomorphism into Aut_K(V); each varphi_sigma is sigma-semilinear; the action is CONTINUOUS (V discrete); equivalently every v in V has OPEN stabilizer; for finite L/K continuity is vacuous
scope_note: v1 RQ-1.16 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: A map phi in Hom_L(V,W) between L-vector spaces with K-structure is K-rational if it commutes with the two given Gal(L/K)-actions on V and W.

hypotheses: V,W L-vector spaces each equipped with a K-structure

enunciation: If V is a K-vector space then L tensor_K V carries a canonical K-structure given by varphi_sigma(alpha tensor v) = sigma(alpha) tensor v, and every K-linear phi: V -> W induces a K-rational map 1 tensor phi.

hypotheses: V a K-vector space
conclusion: the formula defines a K-structure on L tensor_K V; it is canonical; 1 tensor phi is K-rational for every K-linear phi

enunciation: For a quiver with relations, a K-rational structure is required to respect the relations: each Galois element maps a relation to a relation; equivalently the image of rho lies in the automorphism group of the quiver WITH relations.

hypotheses: Gamma a quiver with relations
conclusion: the Galois action permutes the set of relations; equivalently im rho is contained in Aut(Gamma with relations)

enunciation: All isomorphism classes of K-rational structures on a fixed quiver Gamma are classified by H^1(Gal(K^sep/K); Aut(Gamma)), understood as CONTINUOUS cohomology of the profinite group with discrete coefficients (in accordance with the continuity required in def:rationalquivers), with Aut(Gamma) carrying the trivial Galois action WLOG; if Aut(Gamma) is abelian this equals Hom_cont(Gal(K^sep/K), Aut(Gamma)), the group of CONTINUOUS homomorphisms.
hypotheses: Gamma a quiver; L/K Galois
conclusion: the classification by continuous H^1; the identification with Hom_cont in the abelian case

enunciation: Considered over the absolute Galois group, the families (Rep(Gamma_{E'}))_{K subset E' subset K^sep} and (Rep^nil(Gamma_{E'}))_{K subset E' subset K^sep} define stacks in the etale topology on K.
quantifiers: for all intermediate fields K subset E' subset K^sep
hypotheses: Gamma_K a K-rational quiver
conclusion: the two families are stacks in the etale topology on K

enunciation: A K-rational quiver is exactly a diagram E => V (via s and t) in the category of finite continuous discrete Gal(L/K)-sets; i.e. Gabriel's definition reformulated in that category.
hypotheses: Gamma_K a K-rational quiver
conclusion: the data of a K-rational quiver is equivalent to a diagram s,t: E => V of finite Gal(L/K)-sets

enunciation: For infinite L/K the continuity of the semi-linear action, which is part of the definition of a K-structure, is an ESSENTIAL hypothesis of thm:galoisdescent and not a mere convention: a non-continuous semi-linear action of Gal(L/K) on an L-vector space V need not arise via base change from a K-vector space, and the canonical map L tensor_K V^{Gal(L/K)} -> V may fail to be an isomorphism. For finite L/K every semi-linear action is continuous.
quantifiers: for infinite L/K; separately, for finite L/K
hypotheses: L/K a Galois extension; V an L-vector space with a semi-linear Gal(L/K)-action
conclusion: continuity is essential, not conventional, when L/K is infinite; a non-continuous action need not be of base-change form; the canonical map L tensor_K V^{Gal(L/K)} -> V may FAIL to be an isomorphism; for FINITE L/K every semi-linear action is automatically continuous

enunciation: Specifically, a K-rational structure rho on Gamma = (V,E,s,t) is given by (i) a continuous left Gal(L/K)-action rho_V on V and (ii) a continuous left Gal(L/K)-action rho_E on E such that s and t are homomorphisms of Gal(L/K)-sets, s(sigma e) = sigma s(e) and t(sigma e) = sigma t(e) (eq:stgaloisequivariance); Gabriel's definition reformulated in the category of continuous discrete Gal(L/K)-sets.
quantifiers: for all sigma in Gal(L/K) and all e in E
hypotheses: rho a K-rational structure (RQ2-1.02)
conclusion: the componentwise description (rho_V, rho_E, eq:stgaloisequivariance)

enunciation: A K-species S=(L_i, {}_iM_j)_{i,j in I} is a finite collection (L_i) of division rings containing K in their centre, together with an L_i,L_j-bimodule {}_iM_j for each pair i,j on which the left and right K-vector-space structures agree and which is finite-dimensional over K.
quantifiers: for each i,j in I; I finite
hypotheses: I a finite index set
conclusion: each L_i is a division ring containing K in its CENTRE; each {}_iM_j is an L_i,L_j-bimodule; the two induced K-structures on {}_iM_j agree; {}_iM_j is finite-dimensional over K

enunciation: An etale K-species is a K-species S=(L_i,{}_iM_j) in which each L_i is a finite separable extension of K and each {}_iM_j is a commutative L_i tensor_K L_j-algebra which is finite etale as a K-algebra, the L_i,L_j-bimodule structure being the one induced by the algebra structure; equivalently, {}_iM_j is a commutative finite etale K-algebra with two K-algebra homomorphisms L_i -> {}_iM_j <- L_j, its left and right STRUCTURE MAPS.
quantifiers: for each i,j in I
hypotheses: S a K-species
conclusion: each L_i/K is a FINITE SEPARABLE field extension; each {}_iM_j is a COMMUTATIVE L_i tensor_K L_j-ALGEBRA (equivalently a commutative K-algebra with two structure maps); each {}_iM_j is FINITE ETALE as a K-algebra
scope_note: v1 RQ-2.02 CARRIED (CROSSWALK); census-v1.15 cells, tex block MOVED (label added only); v1 history in workflow/census/STATEMENTS.tsv

enunciation: An etale K-species S is split if K is isomorphic to L_i for all i and {}_iM_j is isomorphic to a product of copies of K as K-algebras for all i,j.
quantifiers: for all i,j in I
hypotheses: S an etale K-species
conclusion: K is isomorphic to L_i for all i; {}_iM_j is ISOMORPHIC to product over epsilon of K as K-ALGEBRAS

enunciation: A morphism f: S -> T of etale K-species, S = (L_i,{}_iM_j)_{I}, T = (L~_i,{}_iM~_j)_{I~}, consists of (i) a map iota: I~ -> I of index sets (note the direction), (ii) for each i~ in I~ a K-algebra homomorphism iota_{i~}: L_{iota(i~)} -> L~_{i~}, and (iii) for all s~,t~ in I~ a K-algebra homomorphism iota_{s~t~}: {}_{iota(s~)}M_{iota(t~)} -> {}_{s~}M~_{t~} compatible with the structure maps transported along iota_{s~} and iota_{t~}; composition composes the index maps in the opposite order and the algebra homomorphisms; equivalently (i)+(ii) are a K-algebra homomorphism prod_i L_i -> prod_{i~} L~_{i~} and (iii) compatible edge data.
quantifiers: for each i~ in I~; for all s~,t~ in I~
hypotheses: S,T etale K-species

enunciation: Let E be a subfield of R. The tori K_{D'/E} with D' (x)_E R = C are exactly the E-forms of the real group SO(2); this is not used, only sketched.
